definition: FaceApp is a photo and video editing application for iOS and Android developed by FaceApp Technology Limited, a company based in Cyprus.
details: The app generates highly realistic transformations of human faces in photographs by using neural networks. The app can transform a face to make it smile, look younger, look older, or change gender.

explainer.lead: FaceApp is a photo and video editor for iOS and Android that uses neural networks to make realistic changes to human faces. It matters because transformations such as aging or adding a smile can be produced without manually editing the image.

tiers.eli5: Like a photo filter that can make a picture of you smile, look older, or look younger with one tap.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat it as a real-world consumer application of neural networks that generates highly realistic transformations of human faces in photographs. A practical concern is that edits are convincing, so consent and authenticity of altered photos matter.
tiers.paperLevel: It is defined as an iOS and Android photo and video editing application using neural networks to transform faces, for example to smile, look younger, look older, or change gender; no model specification is given.

explainer.example: Given a portrait of a person with a neutral expression, a user can select the smile transformation. FaceApp generates a new version of the portrait in which the person appears to be smiling.

usedIn.name: FaceApp for iOS
usedIn.detail: Photo and video editing with neural-network-based face transformations.

usedIn.name: FaceApp for Android
usedIn.detail: Mobile editing of faces, including age, smile, and gender transformations.

usedIn.name: Portrait photo editing
usedIn.detail: Creating realistic variations of a photographed human face.

explainer.intuition: Instead of requiring someone to redraw a face, FaceApp uses a neural network to generate a requested facial change automatically. Its distinguishing feature is that the resulting transformation is designed to look highly realistic.
howItWorks: A user supplies a photograph or video containing a human face.
The user chooses a transformation, such as smiling, looking younger, looking older, or changing gender.
FaceApp's neural networks generate the corresponding facial transformation.
The app returns the edited photo or video.
explainer.whyItMatters: FaceApp shows how neural networks can turn complex facial editing into a simple mobile-app operation. It makes realistic age, expression, and gender transformations accessible without manual retouching.
misconceptions: It is not limited to still photographs; it also edits videos.
Its described function is transforming faces, not identifying who a person is.
A realistic-looking transformation is generated imagery, not a record of how someone actually looked or will look.

diagram.caption: FaceApp combines an input face with a selected transformation to produce edited media.
